Verify a message signature

Everything is processed locally in your browser. Your public key, message, and signature are never sent over the network.

  • Key format:
    • SPKI defines a standard format for storing public keys.
    • PEM is a file format for storing cryptographic keys and certificates.
  • Signature scheme:
    • PKCS#1 v1.5 / SHA-256: is PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256 explicitly selected as its message digest algorithm.
    • RSA-PSS: is a newer probabilistic RSA signature scheme. It incorporates a random salt and is generally preferred to PKCS1-v1_5 for new RSA-based applications.
    • ECDSA: is an elliptic-curve signature scheme. It provides security comparable to RSA with significantly smaller keys and signatures. It requires both an elliptic curve, such as P-256, and a hash function, such as SHA-256.
    • Ed25519: is a modern elliptic-curve signature scheme based on Edwards curves. Its cryptographic parameters and hashing behavior are largely fixed by the scheme, making it simpler to use correctly. It produces compact keys and signatures and does not require the application to select a separate hash function.
